title: PostHog autocapture element chain leaks data-resume-token past the sanitize_properties scrub
evidence:
<> "posthog.init('"
        <> key
        <> "',{api_host:'/_ph',"
        <> "ui_host:'https://eu.posthog.com',"
        <> "person_profiles:'identified_only',"
        <> "capture_pageview:true,capture_pageleave:true,"
        <> "opt_out_capturing_by_default:true,"
 ... 
        <> "sanitize_properties:function(p){"
        <> "var re=/(\\/(?:resume|draft-erasure)\\/)[^\\s&#/?]+/g;"
        <> "for(var k in p){if(typeof p[k]==='string'){p[k]=p[k].replace(re,'$1<redacted>');}}"
        <> "return p;},"  — and form_pages.gleam:401: attribute("data-resume-token", resume_token),
detail: init leaves autocapture at the SDK default (true). Verified in posthog-js source: the $autocapture element chain includes body, capturing attr__data-resume-token into $elements_chain (string) and $elements (array). The scrub only rewrites top-level strings matching /resume/|/draft-erasure/ — the bare 48-char token never matches, so every consenting resumed applicant's click/change leaks the live PII-read capability to the analytics store.
recommended_fix: Add autocapture:{element_attribute_ignorelist:['data-resume-token']} (or autocapture:false) to the posthog.init config in view_posthog_snippet, and pin it with a snippet-regression test.
